targets.review_note: Equal LIS levels must decrease in value with increasing position. Consequently, the latest earlier position of level a_i-1 is the smallest eligible predecessor and must be smaller than x_i; link it as the parent, using a virtual root for level one. Traverse this forest in preorder with later siblings first and assign increasing values. The nearest-predecessor invariant gives an inversion-maximal realization: every ascending pair in that order is forced by the predecessor chains and the decreasing order within levels. Hence every decreasing subsequence in any other valid realization remains decreasing in this one, so all starting LDS lengths are simultaneously maximized. Compute those lengths by a right-to-left Fenwick maximum query over smaller values and sum them. Bind to the earlier original production checkpoint CP-97fd4e5dda674b3c, where the complete task is already observed, instead of truncating the later25363-token sequence.
